public_rationale: The antecedent happened. Oil-driven inflation led the Fed to raise rates in September 2026, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose about a full point from its February low. After that, AI borrowing did get notably more expensive. Investors sought about 0.4 points more on Meta's El Paso data-center bonds than on the pre-war Hyperion deal. AFP reported that lenders demanded returns from tech giants that would once have been unthinkable. Oracle's credit spread more than doubled during 2026. One caveat: some of the repricing reflects AI-specific credit worries, not just higher rates. But the forecast's outcome, costlier AI financing after rates rose, came true.
limitations: Rate effects and AI-specific credit concerns cannot be cleanly separated.
'Significantly' has no stated threshold. Roughly 0.4 points on a $12 billion deal, plus a doubled Oracle spread, is my reading of significant.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If the Iran war pushes prices and interest rates up, financing the AI bubble's borrowing will become significantly more expensive.
conditions: if oil prices soar and interest rates rise

statement.excerpt: Iran changes that in the most obvious way possible — if prices soar, interest rates may follow, and if rates go up, even by a point or two of a percentage, financing the tens and hundreds of billions of dollars in borrowing that the AI bubble demands will become significantly more expensive.

from_speaker: if prices soar, interest rates may follow
if rates go up, even by a point or two of a percentage
financing the tens and hundreds of billions of dollars in borrowing that the AI bubble demands
our_interpretation: Antecedent: after the post, energy-driven inflation rose and US interest rates went up. A rise of about one percentage point in a benchmark rate such as the 10-year Treasury counts, since he said 'even by a point or two'.
Outcome: borrowing costs on AI-related debt rose noticeably after the post. I measure this by yields and credit spreads paid by AI borrowers such as Oracle and Meta's data-center vehicles.
No deadline was given. A clear, dated repricing of AI debt after the antecedent happened counts as a decisive event.
criteria.support_condition: Rates rose after the war began, and AI-related borrowers then paid clearly higher yields or spreads than before. Examples: new Meta data-center debt priced well above earlier deals, or Oracle spreads widening sharply.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Rates rose, but AI borrowers kept getting financing at the same or lower yields and spreads than before.

evidence.excerpt: The Federal Reserve on Wednesday approved its first interest rate hike in more than three years and indicated another is to come, as part of an effort aimed at combating inflation brought on by spiraling oil prices and other factors.
evidence.explanation: Shows that prices rose on oil and that the Fed responded by raising rates, which is the antecedent.

evidence.excerpt: The benchmark is up about a full percentage point since its February low.
evidence.locator: section 'Fed rarely moves once', paragraph on Treasury yields
evidence.explanation: The 10-year benchmark rose about one percentage point, which meets his 'a point or two' threshold.

evidence.excerpt: Early discussions point to yields above 7%, with some investors seeking roughly 0.4 percentage points more than on Meta's Hyperion project
evidence.explanation: A new Meta data-center financing cost clearly more than the comparable pre-war Hyperion deal.

evidence.excerpt: they have demanded returns that would have been unthinkable for such blue-chip companies not long ago.
evidence.explanation: Reports that lenders charged AI borrowers much higher returns in 2026. The same article ties higher US borrowing costs to war-driven inflation.

evidence.excerpt: At the same time Oracle's spread rose to 308.25 basis points on Oct. 21, up from 141 on Jan. 2.
evidence.locator: section 'Insurance costs rise for AI-linked debt'
evidence.explanation: Oracle's credit spread more than doubled in 2026, a sign its debt became more costly to finance.

evidence.excerpt: What has shifted is how much protection the market wants against project-specific risk sitting one step removed from Meta’s balance sheet
evidence.locator: section 'Why the market has started pricing AI debt differently'
evidence.explanation: Puts part of the repricing down to AI-specific risk and supply, not only higher rates. This weakens the causal link but not the cost rise.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: After a roughly one-point rise in the 10-year yield, a Meta-linked data-center financing was priced about 0.4 points above the comparable pre-war deal.
